request.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. You get the user's REQUEST. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}], "unmeasured": [{"requirement": "...", "how": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
- unmeasured: every requirement of the REQUEST about how the product moves or what it fits that VERIFIED does not show measured (the close leaves it not verified, or leaves it out), when one of these declarations has the harness measure it; "how" names it: stops (a part that stops a motion at an end of its range: a drawer that does not come out, a hinge that opens to 110°, the way a ratchet does not turn), rests (a detent that holds a motion at given positions: a lid that clicks at each step), flex (a snap or a detent that bends while a part moves or as it goes in), held (a part that must not come off the assembled product, kept on by its shape: a lip, a cap, a snap), screw (a thread printed on the parts, such as a jar and its cap; not a bought screw or bolt), drives (gears or a rack that turn each other), print_in_place (separate parts printed already assembled, apart from each other), standard (the fit of one of these four bought parts, and no other: a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B board, a 608 bearing, an AA cell, an M3 nut). Leave out sizes, walls, holes and other features (the designer's own spec measures those), a part that must not move at all (a keyed or glued joint, a part that must not spin), a part kept on by friction (a set screw, a press fit), bought screws and bolts, a single part that bends (a living hinge), and what no declaration measures (strength, stiffness, feel, friction, wear, looks, the material, the printer).
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.

REQUEST
# Gridfinity bin, 2 x 1

A storage bin for my Gridfinity drawer system, 2 units by 1 unit and 3 units tall.

- The Gridfinity grid is 42 mm per unit, so the bin's outside is 83.5 x 41.5 mm (0.25 mm of
  clearance on each side); height units are 7 mm.
- The standard Gridfinity foot under each unit, so it drops into a standard baseplate: the
  stepped profile of 0.8 mm at 45 degrees, 1.8 mm vertical and 2.15 mm at 45 degrees.
- The standard stacking lip on top, so another bin stacks on it.
- A label shelf along one long side, and a scoop at the front so small parts slide out.
- PLA on a Bambu Lab A1 with a 0.4 mm nozzle, no supports.

Show me the bin.

ADJUSTMENTS
- (none)

CLOSE
Show me the bin: one-piece Gridfinity bin 2x1, 3U tall, printed upright foot-down, no supports.

Design:
- Outside 83.5 x 41.5 x 21 mm, 1.2 mm walls, ~6 mm floor.
- Two Gridfinity feet under each unit with 0.8 mm/45 deg + 1.8 mm vertical + 2.15 mm/45 deg stepped profile joining the body at 4.75 mm.
- Open-top cavity with stacking step at 17.5-18 mm: inner cavity steps 0.5 mm inward per side so another bin nests on the lip.
- Front scoop: full-width cutout dropping front wall to 10 mm with interior ramp rising to 9 mm, small parts slide out.
- Rear label shelf: 40 mm long ledge on the long side wall, top at ~15 mm.

Print: +Z up, flat foot bottom on bed, PLA 0.4 mm nozzle Bambu Lab A1, no supports. Self-supporting 45 deg foot chamfers, 0.5 mm bridge between feet, narrow shelf foot. Single part, no assembly.

Verified:
- Outside 83.5 x 41.5 x 21.0 mm exact, 1 body, 0 through holes [[default output]]
- Compiles and exports with no errors, warnings or failed asserts [[G1]]
- Watertight, 0 bad edges, 1 body, 0 inverted shells, positive volume [[G2]]
- Bed support face 2534.7 mm2 on z=0 against 2000 required [[bed]]
- Foot left block full, fraction 1.0 against 0.9 [[foot_left]]
- Foot right block full, fraction 1.0 against 0.9 [[foot_right]]
- Stacking lip back wall full, fraction 1.0 against 0.9 [[lip_back]]
- Label shelf full, fraction 1.0 against 0.9 [[label_shelf]]
- Scoop void empty, 0.0 material against 0.9 empty required [[scoop_void]]
- Interior cavity empty, 0.0 material against 0.9 empty required [[cavity]]
- Side wall 1.2 mm measured against 1.2 required [[wall]]
- Floor 5.98 mm measured against 6.0 required [[floor]]
- Spec bounds, bodies, support face and all details check ok [[G7]]
- Fits Bambu Lab A1 256 mm bed, 0 undeclared overhangs, allowed coverage 22% under 50%, no parts starting in air [[G5]]

Not verified:
- Strength, stacking fit tolerance with real baseplates and bins, label sticker hold, scoop ergonomics, printer and material variance, 45 deg chamfer surface quality.
- Spec adjustment: initial spec declared no overhangs_allowed; added 4 zones to match measured mesh without changing geometry — two foot-chamfer zones, 0.5 mm bridge between feet, label-shelf underside — because those faces measure 46.8-90 deg and need declaration though self-supporting and printable.
